clauses.anchor: Report 1 s2: before tracking starts, `confogl_addcvar` stages assignments without changing live ConVars
Report 1 s3: names are case-insensitive and the last valid assignment wins, for existing and pending ConVars
Report 1 s4: duplicate assignments must not create duplicate hooks or reset records
clauses.note: Observed only indirectly through the later enforcement/restore values.

clauses.anchor: Report 1 s5: once tracking has started, further add commands remain ignored
Report 2 s1-2: on the first effective `confogl_setcvars`, capture each resolvable ConVar's actual value immediately before the batch writes; registration-time values are not baselines
Report 2 s3: snapshot the whole batch before any write (another plugin's change hook may change a second ConVar)
Report 2 s4: repeated activation/config callbacks must not replace a baseline with an enforced value
clauses.note: Observed through the late-entry restore cases.

clauses.anchor: Report 2 s5: "Keep the existing match-enabled gate."
clauses.note: Only the reset half of the gate is exercised (R5.5).

clauses.anchor: Report 3 s1: while active, an external change is corrected to the staged desired value synchronously
Report 3 s2: respect SourceMod's normal bound/coercion behaviour (desired 20 with upper bound 10 enforces 10)
Report 3 s3-4: no infinite recursion, no duplicate registrations, no global skip of other tracked ConVars during a hook callback; a finite cross-ConVar callback leaves no drift
Report 3 s5-6: an in-range desired string retains its representation (`01`), including after finite cross-ConVar writeback
Report 4 s1-2: unresolved names survive configuration callbacks; when they first resolve, capture their value at first activation and enforce them like early entries
Report 4 s3: a callback while inactive only resolves/stages entries
Report 4 s4: later repeated callbacks preserve the first baseline; resolution and duplicate staging never produce two records for one ConVar
Report 5 s1-2: `confogl_resetcvars` (match disabled) and plugin unload release the whole profile, removing hooks before restoring each activated entry's saved string exactly
Report 5 s3: discard pending/staged records; an entry that was never activated writes nothing on release
Report 5 s4: a later profile cycle captures a fresh baseline
Report 5 s5: a reset while a match is enabled remains rejected without changing state
Report 6 s1-2: keep the 63-byte maximum for names and values; reject oversized arguments in full, including an oversized duplicate, without truncating or overwriting a previous valid assignment
Report 6 s3: empty desired strings and quoted strings with spaces remain valid
Report 6 s4: preserve restoration baselines up to 255 bytes without truncation
Report 7: `confogl_cvarsettings`/`confogl_cvardiff` handle negative, end-of-list and past-end offsets without exception or mutation; valid pages keep their behaviour
clauses.note: Valid-page output is not compared; only absence of an exception and an unchanged profile are observed.

clauses.anchor: Closing paragraph: public commands, native declarations and other modules remain compatible
clauses.note: Only the confogl_* commands used by the suite and sm_resetmatch are exercised.

known_issues: benchmarks/l4d2-core/private/harbor/l4d2-confogl-cvar-transactions-hard/tests/verify.py:parse_suite: a suite boot is all-or-nothing. Any "[SM] Exception reported", "Native is not bound" or "Plugin ... failed to load" line, a missing FINAL marker or a duplicate case turns EVERY case of that boot into a failure, including cases that would otherwise pass; read per-case outcomes of a failing boot with that in mind.

The unchanged starter throws inside confogl_cvardiff (Invalid index -1) during the single suite boot, so all 42 cases fail closed. No case has a passing starter baseline: there is no preserved set and no compat-negative control for this task. Roles are therefore 'target' for every case by observation; clauses that the exam states as preservation (R6.2, R7.1 valid pages) are still only target evidence here.
The alternative control is reference-derived (reverse batch order and strcmp); it is not an independent implementation.
